content:
DRAFT — Outreach Sequences + Email Copy
Redwood Inference | Customer Case Study + Reference Program (Design Partners)

Owner: Camila Reyes (Marketing)
Messaging lead: Soojin Lee (Product Marketing)
Sales/CS users: AEs + CSMs + SE support

Goal of these templates
- Recruit 3–5 design partners willing to participate in:
  (1) Public case study (web + PDF) with quantified outcomes + architecture details (within what’s safe)
  (2) Scheduled reference calls for qualified prospects
- Create consistent asks, set expectations, and reduce back-and-forth during legal/comms approval.

Program snapshot (for internal context)
- Time commitment: ~2 interviews (45–60 min each) + async review + 1 final approval step
- Timeline: ~8–10 weeks end-to-end, but we can publish earlier for lightweight stories
- What Redwood provides: draft narrative, design, metrics validation support, review/approval process, reference-call scheduling & prep
- What we ask the customer for:
  - Named champion/spokesperson + reviewer in Legal/Comms (or equivalent)
  - Approval to use logo + 1–3 quotes (release form)
  - Confirmation of metrics & measurement window (p50/p95 latency, cost/token or cost/query, reliability/error rate, throughput)

Personalization tokens (use consistently)
- {{FirstName}}, {{LastName}}, {{Title}}, {{Company}}
- {{UseCase}} (e.g., regulated clinical summarization, fintech fraud triage, SaaS doc search)
- {{DeploymentMode}} (Hosted / Dedicated / Private)
- {{Outcome1}}, {{Outcome2}} (keep specific; avoid over-claiming)
- {{RedwoodContact}} (AE/CSM)
- {{SEContact}} (if technical validation is needed)
- {{ProposedTimeline}} (e.g., “June interview, publish in July”)
- {{ReleaseFormLink}} (Drive/DocSign link — TBD by Legal)

Do / Don’t (quick guardrails)
DO
- Be explicit about what participation means (interviews, draft review, final approval)
- Offer 3 options: (A) public case study + references, (B) references-only, (C) anonymized story
- Name the value back to them (recruiting, credibility, thought leadership, marketplace visibility)
- Keep metrics phrasing careful (“observed in their workload,” “during a 30-day window,” “p95 under X ms in their POC environment”)

DON’T
- Don’t imply guaranteed performance across all workloads
- Don’t mention other customers by name unless already public and approved
- Don’t ask them to share sensitive architecture/security details (keys, network diagrams with internal IP ranges, vendor lists under NDA)
- Don’t promise a specific publish date until we have an approver and validation owner


SEQUENCE 1 — Existing customer: Invite to be a design partner (case study + references)
Audience: Customers already in production / high-confidence POC results
Owner: AE (with CSM CC after first positive response)

Email 1 (Day 1) — “The ask”
Subject options:
- {{Company}} + Redwood: would you be open to a short case study?
- Invite: design partner for Redwood’s customer story + reference program
- Quick ask (15 min): featuring {{Company}}’s {{UseCase}} on Redwood

Body:
Hi {{FirstName}},

You’ve built one of the most compelling Redwood deployments we’ve seen for {{UseCase}} (especially given {{Constraint}}). We’re putting together a small set of 3–5 “design partner” customer stories focused on real production outcomes (latency/cost/reliability + deployment learnings).

Would {{Company}} be open to participating?

What it involves (we’ll do the heavy lifting):
1) 45–60 min interview (you + optionally someone from Eng/Platform)
2) We draft a 2–4 page case study (web + PDF) + a lightweight architecture diagram
3) You review/redline and give final approval (including logo/quote release)
4) Optional: join 1–2 reference calls per quarter for qualified prospects (we handle scheduling + prep)

Why teams do this:
- Highlight engineering wins publicly (recruiting + credibility)
- Influence roadmap (we treat design partners as “fast lane” for feedback)
- Optional co-marketing moment (e.g., marketplace listing, webinar, blog)

If you’re open, could we do a 15-min kickoff next week to confirm what’s publishable and who needs to approve on your side?

{{RedwoodContact}}
Title | Redwood Inference

PS: If public isn’t possible, we can do a reference-only option or an anonymized story.


Follow-up 1 (Day 4)
Subject: Re: featuring {{Company}}’s {{UseCase}} on Redwood

Hi {{FirstName}} — quick bump. Happy to keep it lightweight:
- Public case study + logo + 1 quote (best)
- Reference calls only (no public assets)
- Anonymized story (no logo/name)

Which option is easiest for your team right now?

{{RedwoodContact}}


Follow-up 2 (Day 8)
Subject: Should I close the loop on this?

Hi {{FirstName}},

Should I close the loop on the design partner invite, or is there someone else at {{Company}} (Comms/Legal/Marketing) I should coordinate with?

If helpful, we can send a one-page outline + example structure to make approvals easier.

Thanks,
{{RedwoodContact}}


If they say “yes” (reply template)
Subject: Great — next steps for {{Company}}’s case study + references

Amazing — thank you.

Next steps:
1) Can you confirm the best point person(s) for:
   - Technical interview (platform/ML/infra)
   - Legal/comms approval (logo + quote)
2) Do you have any constraints on what we can publish? (examples: deployment mode wording, regions, model names, compliance language)
3) We’ll send:
   - Interview agenda + metrics checklist
   - Draft timeline ({{ProposedTimeline}})

Tentative kickoff slots:
- {{TimeOption1}}
- {{TimeOption2}}

{{RedwoodContact}}
(CC {{CSMName}}; {{SEContact}} for metrics validation)


If they say “maybe later” (snooze template)
Subject: Re: design partner invite — timing

Totally understood. What timing would be better to revisit?

Common triggers:
- After a stable production window (e.g., 30 days)
- After a major feature launch (rollouts, fallback policies, Private deployment milestone)

If you share a rough month, I’ll set a reminder and keep it off your plate until then.

{{RedwoodContact}}



SEQUENCE 2 — POC prospect: Conditional case study agreement (when targets are met)
Audience: Active POC where customer expressed interest in participating if results are strong
Owner: AE + SE (send jointly or AE send w/ SE on CC)

Email — “Conditional yes” framing
Subject options:
- Quick add-on to our POC plan (customer story option)
- If we hit the POC targets: would you consider a case study?

Body:
Hi {{FirstName}},

As we finalize the POC plan for {{UseCase}}, I wanted to float an optional (but valuable) add-on.

If Redwood meets the agreed success criteria ({{POCMetric1}}, {{POCMetric2}}) in your POC environment, would {{Company}} be open to either:
A) a public case study (logo + 1–3 quotes), and/or
B) serving as a reference for a small number of qualified prospects?

We’ll keep it simple:
- 1 interview during/after the POC
- We draft everything
- You approve final wording (and can restrict what is public)

If you’re open, we can document the “conditional yes” now so it’s not a scramble later.

Thanks,
{{RedwoodContact}}


POC follow-up — “Approval path” (send once they agree)
Subject: Who should approve a customer story at {{Company}}?

Hi {{FirstName}},

To make sure we don’t slow you down later, who would need to approve:
- Use of {{Company}} logo
- 1–3 attributed quotes (name/title)
- A short write-up of the architecture at a high level

If you share the right contacts, we’ll route the release form early and keep the process low-friction.

{{RedwoodContact}}



SEQUENCE 3 — Reference-call-only ask (lightweight)
Audience: Customers willing to help but not ready for public marketing
Owner: CSM (preferred) or AE (if AE-led account)

Email 1
Subject options:
- Quick request: occasional reference calls (we’ll do the prep)
- Would you be open to helping 1–2 peer teams evaluating Redwood?

Body:
Hi {{FirstName}},

We have a small number of teams evaluating Redwood for {{UseCase}} / {{DeploymentMode}} and your experience would be incredibly helpful.

Would you be open to doing occasional reference calls (typically 30 minutes, 1–2 per quarter), with clear boundaries?
- We’ll send a short prep sheet with context + topics to cover/avoid
- You can always decline if timing is bad
- We can keep it “reference-only” (no public logo/quotes)

If yes, what topics are you comfortable speaking to?
- Latency/throughput and performance tuning
- Reliability (fallbacks, error handling)
- Deployment/security requirements (at a high level)
- Developer experience (integration, docs, support)

Thank you,
{{CSMName}}
Customer Success | Redwood Inference


Follow-up (Day 5)
Subject: Re: occasional reference calls

Hi {{FirstName}} — following up. Even a single call can help a lot.

If you’re open, can you share preferred windows (e.g., Tue/Thu afternoons) and any hard no-go topics?

{{CSMName}}


Internal note (not customer-facing):
- If they agree, create/update HubSpot: Reference readiness = “Yes — reference only”
- Add boundaries + preferred scheduling windows in the account record



SEQUENCE 4 — Public case study ask (post-success moment)
Use when: After a strong result (metrics improvement, Private deployment milestone, big launch)
Owner: AE or CSM; add Marketing (Ethan Wallace) after initial yes

Email — “Celebrate + invite”
Subject options:
- Congrats on {{Milestone}} — would you be open to sharing the story?
- Could we draft a public write-up of your {{UseCase}} results?

Body:
Hi {{FirstName}},

Congrats again on {{Milestone}} — the way your team handled {{Constraint}} was genuinely impressive.

Would {{Company}} be open to a public case study? We’d like to highlight:
- The challenge + constraints ({{Constraint}})
- What you implemented (high-level architecture, deployment mode, routing/fallback if relevant)
- Outcomes you observed (e.g., {{Outcome1}}, {{Outcome2}} — we’ll validate carefully)

We’ll do the writing/design and keep approvals in your control. If you prefer, we can:
- exclude specific vendor names
- avoid exact numbers (use ranges)
- keep some sections “high level” for security

If you’re open, I’ll connect you with our writer (Ethan Wallace) to schedule the interview and share the metrics checklist.

Thanks,
{{RedwoodContact}}



SEQUENCE 5 — Legal/Comms approval kickoff (introduce release + avoid surprises)
Audience: Customer legal/comms contact
Owner: Marketing (Camila or Ethan) with AE/CSM CC

Email — “Approval package”
Subject options:
- Approval workflow for {{Company}} x Redwood case study (logo/quotes)
- Materials for review: {{Company}} customer story + release form

Body:
Hi {{ApproverName}},

I’m reaching out because {{FirstName}} is exploring participation in Redwood Inference’s customer story + reference program.

We want to make review easy and ensure we stay within your guidelines. Our standard package includes:
- Draft case study (Google Doc) for redlines
- List of proposed approved quotes (attributed; names/titles optional)
- List of specific claims/metrics we intend to publish (with measurement window)
- Logo usage scope (website + PDF; no paid ads unless separately approved)
- Release form for signature: {{ReleaseFormLink}}

We can also support constraints like:
- anonymized story (no name/logo)
- “no exact metrics” (use ranges)
- pre-approved security language

What’s the best way to run approvals at {{Company}} (single approver vs. sequential Legal + Comms)?

Thank you,
{{MarketingSender}}
Redwood Inference | Product Marketing
CC: {{RedwoodContact}}, {{CSMName}}


If they request changes to release terms (internal placeholder reply)
Subject: Re: Release form redlines — {{Company}}

Thanks — we can accommodate reasonable redlines. I’m looping in our counsel (Sofia Mendes) to review and propose edits quickly.

Could you also confirm:
- Who is the final signatory?
- Any brand guidelines we should follow for logo usage?
- Whether spokesperson attribution (name/title) is required or optional?

{{MarketingSender}}



SEQUENCE 6 — Interview scheduling + prep (engineering-friendly)
Audience: Engineering/platform stakeholder and champion
Owner: Ethan Wallace (writer) or AE/CSM if writer not introduced yet

Email — “Interview invite”
Subject options:
- 45 min interview: capturing {{Company}}’s {{UseCase}} deployment on Redwood
- Case study interview + metrics validation ({{Company}} x Redwood)

Body:
Hi {{FirstName}},

Thanks again for being open to the customer story. The interview is straightforward and engineering-first.

Agenda (45–60 min):
1) Use case + traffic shape (what changed when you went to production)
2) Constraints (security, data retention, regions, latency targets)
3) Architecture (high level): {{DeploymentMode}}, routing/fallback, caching/batching, model selection, rollouts
4) Outcomes + how you measured (we’ll validate with you/your team)
5) What you’d tell another team evaluating inference platforms

Prep (optional, but helpful):
- Any screenshots/dashboards you’re comfortable sharing internally (latency p50/p95, cost/query, error rates)
- Measurement window you consider “representative”

Suggested times:
- {{TimeOption1}}
- {{TimeOption2}}

Best,
Ethan Wallace
Customer stories | Redwood Inference
CC: {{RedwoodContact}}, {{SEContact}}



SEQUENCE 7 — Draft review nudge (keep approvals moving)
Audience: Champion + approver
Owner: Marketing (Ethan) with AE/CSM in CC

Email — “Review request”
Subject options:
- Draft ready for review — {{Company}} x Redwood case study
- Can you redline by {{Date}}? (happy to adjust)

Body:
Hi {{FirstName}},

Sharing the first draft here: {{DraftLink}}.

What we need from you:
- Confirm factual accuracy (architecture, deployment details)
- Confirm approved metrics/phrasing (we can remove exact numbers if preferred)
- Confirm quote attribution (name/title) OR request anonymous attribution
- Confirm any “do not mention” topics

If it helps, you can reply with:
- “Approved as-is,” or
- Bullet changes, or
- Edits directly in the doc

Is {{ReviewDueDate}} feasible? If not, tell me what date works and we’ll adjust the publishing timeline.

Thanks,
Ethan


Follow-up (Day 5 after sharing draft)
Subject: Re: draft for review — any blockers?

Hi {{FirstName}},

Quick check: any blockers to reviewing the draft this week? We can also jump on a 15-min call and walk through changes live.

Thanks,
Ethan



SEQUENCE 8 — Reference call request to customer (after they opt in)
Audience: Customer reference participant
Owner: CSM (preferred) + AE if deal-critical

Email — “Specific request”
Subject options:
- Reference call request (30 min) — {{ProspectCompany}} evaluating {{DeploymentMode}}
- Quick peer chat request (Redwood evaluation)

Body:
Hi {{FirstName}},

We have a qualified prospect, {{ProspectCompany}}, evaluating Redwood for {{ProspectUseCase}}. Would you be open to a 30-minute reference call?

Proposed times:
- {{TimeOption1}}
- {{TimeOption2}}

We’ll send a short prep sheet in advance with:
- Prospect context and what they care about
- Suggested topics
- Topics to avoid (per your guidance)

Call format:
- 5 min intros
- 20 min Q&A
- 5 min wrap

Thank you — we really appreciate it.

{{CSMName}}


If customer asks “what should we say / what not to say?” (reply template)
Subject: Re: reference call boundaries

Great question — here are the recommended boundaries:
OK topics:
- Integration experience (SDK/API, streaming)
- How you approached reliability + fallback (at a high level)
- What improved for you and in what context (measurement window)
- What you wish you’d known early

Avoid:
- Any confidential customer data or internal security details
- Any non-public vendor pricing
- Any unreleased Redwood roadmap

I’ll also share a 1-page prep doc tailored to this call.

{{CSMName}}



SEQUENCE 9 — Inbound interest (customer replies positively to content / asks about co-marketing)
Audience: Inbound leads or customers who ask about being featured
Owner: Growth/Marketing or AE, depending on relationship

Email — “Qualify + route”
Subject: Re: featuring {{Company}} on Redwood

Hi {{FirstName}},

Yes — we’d love to explore a customer story.

A few quick questions to route this correctly:
1) Are you open to public logo + company name, or do you prefer anonymized?
2) Which deployment mode are you using (Hosted / Dedicated / Private)?
3) What outcomes are you most excited to share? (latency, cost/query, reliability, deployment constraints)
4) Who would need to approve anything public (Comms/Legal/Marketing)?

If you reply with short answers, I’ll propose next steps and get the right team looped in.

Thanks,
{{SenderName}}



SEQUENCE 10 — “No public, but yes to anonymized” option
Audience: Customers with strict comms constraints
Owner: AE/CSM

Email
Subject: Option: anonymized customer story (no logo, no name)

Hi {{FirstName}},

Understood on the publicity constraints. We can still capture the learnings as an anonymized story:
- No company name/logo
- No identifiable architecture details
- Optional: ranges instead of exact metrics

This still helps peers understand what “good” looks like and reduces repetitive questions in sales cycles.

Would you be open to a 45-minute interview and a quick review/approval step?

{{RedwoodContact}}



Add-ons / snippets (drop into any email)

Value prop snippet (for engineering champions)
- “We’ll focus on what engineers care about: deployment constraints, integration, reliability patterns, and measurable outcomes (with careful measurement notes).”

Value prop snippet (for comms/marketing stakeholders)
- “We can align on narrative + brand guidelines, and we won’t publish without explicit written approval. You can restrict channels (website/PDF only), exclude paid usage, and require final sign-off.”

Metrics safety snippet
- “We’ll phrase metrics as ‘observed by {{Company}} in their workload during {{Window}}’ and include relevant qualifiers (traffic shape, model version, deployment mode).”


Open questions / TODOs (internal)
- Confirm standard release form link + process (DocuSign vs Google Drive signature) — Legal
- Confirm standard SLA language we’re allowed to reference (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private) — PMM + Legal
- Decide default stance on including model names (allowed? optional?) — PMM + Security
- Build a 1-page “what’s included” PDF to attach to first outreach? (optional)
- HubSpot automation: after a positive response, auto-create task for Marketing intro + add reference readiness fields

Change log (lightweight)
- 2025-06-16: Added reference-call-only sequence; added legal/comms approval kickoff template; added anonymized option email.
- 2025-06-02: Updated design partner invite to include time commitment + options (public/reference-only/anonymized).
